newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-GENTLEMAN VALDANO RETURNS TO BERNABEU STADIUM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GENTLEMAN VALDANO RETURNS TO BERNABEU STADIUM.

text.p: Jorge Valdano resumes his managerial career this weekend by leading Valencia against the club where he made his name as both player and manager, Real Madrid.
The elegant and eloquent Argentine says he won't sit on the bench for Sunday's game out of respect for his predecessor Luis Aragones, who resigned on Tuesday.

But few doubt it is Valdano, and not caretaker manager Jose Manuel Rielo, who is calling the shots ahead of the clash, which also pits Real striker Predrag Mijatovic against his former Valencia team mates.
A World Cup winner with Argentina in 1986, Valdano played a key role in the Real side that dominated the Spanish game in the late 1980s, winning five consecutive league titles.
He showed the same vision and intelligence as manager at Tenerife, transforming the Canary Islanders from relegation candidates into a side capable of knocking big names out of the UEFA Cup.

The step up to the coach's seat at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium was only a matter of time, and Valdano disappointed nobody when he took Real to an impressive championship triumph in his first season in charge in 1994-95.
Valdano's team played an open, attacking game inspired by Dane Michael Laudrup and Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano, and Real drew many admirers.
Off the field, Spanish sports journalists used to jotting down monosyllables were dazzled by the extensive vocabulary and verbal coherence of a man who is generous in victory as well as defeat.
But Valdano needed all of his win-or-lose equanimity as things went badly wrong last season after a summer in which financial problems prevented Real from signing new players.
Valdano left this January on terms so amicable that club president Lorenzo Sanz seemed almost apologetic when announcing his dismissal.
It was a tone that was only fitting in dealing with Valdano, who had literally apologised after his Tenerife side knocked Real out of the Spanish Cup three years previously.
Valdano's Valencia will face another modern-day exponent of old-fashioned values on Sunday, Croatian Euro 96 forward Davor Suker.
The former Sevilla striker refused to celebrate after scoring in last Sunday's 3-1 victory at his old club, and has even taken a recent severe allergic reaction in good heart.
"I'm Sukerman, so I'm allergic to certain metals," he joked, alluding to the film character Superman's allergy to kryptonite.
Suker's good humour is not shared by Balkan strike partner Predrag Mijatovic, the dominant figure in Valencia's charge to second place in last year's championship.
"If I score a goal I will celebrate it," the Montenegrin said. "In Valencia I don't owe anybody anything."
Nevertheless, Mijatovic was generous in his praise for both Aragones and his replacement.
"Taking the place of Luis will be very difficult but Valdano is the best they could have signed," he said.
